title: Phantom Crash
subtitle: Old Tokyo hosts a mechanical combat sport
summary: Phantom Crash is Genki's Xbox vehicular combat game, first released in Japan on 20 June 2002. body: Phantom Crash is Genki's Xbox vehicular combat game, first released in Japan on 20 June 2002. In 2031, the abandoned streets of Old Tokyo have become arenas for a televised sport called Rumbling. The player arrives as an unknown competitor and attempts to climb its rankings in a customisable Scoot Vehicle. Winning a fight produces money for repairs and new parts, connecting success in the arena to the machine used in the next event. Conversations and shop visits place that mechanical career within a small community of rival pilots.

Arms, shoulders, legs and bodies can be changed, allowing the player to combine different weapons and handling characteristics. Event weight limits make equipment a choice rather than a list of upgrades to install indiscriminately. Optical camouflage briefly hides the vehicle, while rocket-assisted jumps add another way to cross the arena or escape an attack. Damage carries repair costs, so surviving efficiently matters alongside defeating competitors. A successful configuration needs to suit the player's movement and the restrictions of the event, turning the garage into a practical extension of each fight.

Quest Mode advances through a day-to-day structure, with an event, shopping and story encounters reached through a map. Class captains provide milestones as the player works through the competitive ranks. Custom paint and the vehicle's personality-giving CHIPs add expression to the mechanical choices, while the soundtrack gives Rumbling a contemporary urban character. Reviews responded to the detailed machines and customisation, though the limited arenas and extensive dialogue divided opinion. Genki later revisited the idea in S.L.A.I., carrying the relationship between pilots, configurable machines and televised combat onto PlayStation 2.
